newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European shares, Wall Street bubble higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European shares, Wall Street bubble higher.

text.p: European share markets drove into new territory on Wednesday, with London, Frankfurt and Amsterdam scaling new peaks, while the dollar hit levels not seen against the yen in more than 2-1/2 years.
The dollar's strength and strong opening trade on Wall Street gave European financial markets decisive support.
London shares brushed past 4,000 points on the blue chip FTSE 100 index for the first time, Frankfurt closed bourse trade at a record high and takeover fever pushed Amsterdam to a trading peak.

Europe's other major equity market, Paris, pushed forward more than one percent by mid-afternoon. Hong Kong had its best finish this year, the Australian stock market ended at a five-month high and Budapest posted its second straight record.
The dollar briefly drove through the key 112 yen level in the European afternoon for its best performance against the Japanese currency since January 24, 1994.
The dollar's surge in the last few days has been the result, traders said, of talk of increased flows of funds from Japan.

"What we're seeing is a continued realisation that the Japanese trade position is in pretty dire straits, and that the fundamentals point in the direction of a weaker yen," said Nigel Richardson, international economist at Yamaichi International.
By 1400 GMT the dollar was quoted around 111.88 yen and 1.5274 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
Overnight comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that there were no threats to inflation down the track added to the upbeat mood in Europe.
London's blue chip FTSE 100 index shot through 4,000 points at the opening, then powered to a high of 4,014.4 in early trade, topping its previous best of 3,994.1 set on September 20.
A slackening of buying pressure pegged the index back a few points through the morning, but the Dow's strong opening sent the FTSE back close to its high.

London's share traders said an influx of cash at the start of the new quarter, combined with moderate growth and benign inflationary pressures in Britain and the United States provided the backdrop for the stock market's heady rise in recent days.
But frothy share prices on both sides of the Atlantic gave some traders pause for thought.

"We remain cautious looking into next year," said Nomura strategist Nick Knight, "both as a function of our concerns regarding the U.S. and more particulary with regard to UK monetary policy post the election."
Germany's DAX index surged to another record high, buoyed by Wall Street gains ahead of Thursday's German national reunification holiday.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade up 20.77 points at 2,676.50 after hitting a trading record at 2,680.10, which surpassed the old level set on September 26 at 2,672.59.
"There's no wonder why the market keeps moving higher when you look at the dollar and Wall Street," one trader said.
Although some traders said there was a risk of profit-taking in post-bourse IBIS computer dealings, the IBIS DAX index was holding up at 2,679.41 at 1400 GMT.
French shares extended their gains through the day, swept higher by advances made by other European stock markets and a firm bond market.
By mid-afternoon, the blue chip CAC-40 index was up 19.36 points or 0.91 percent, at 2,142.57.
Traders reported strong interest from foreign buyers who were anxious not to miss out on the market's rise.
"Everyone's looking at the Bourse through rose-tinted spectacles. We've forgotten the budget and strikes," said one trader.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 111.88 yen and 1.5274 marks versus Tuesday's late European levels of 111.40 and 1.5261.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was up 20.2 points at 4,012.4.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index of German shares closed floor trade up 20.77 at 2,676.50. The IBIS DAX was at 2,679.41 in late screen-based trade
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 19.36 at 2,142.57.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed stronger at $380.30 against $379.20 in the morning and London's close on Tuesday of of $378.65. Silver was two cents firmer at $4.93.
